Declare a hypothesis test

Source: R/declare_estimator.R
declare_test.Rd

Like declare_estimator() but the result table does not gain an inquiry column; intended for tests not tied to an estimand.

Usage

declare_test(
  ...,
  .method = NULL,
  .summary = tidy_try,
  term = NULL,
  label = "test",
  handler = NULL,
  draws = 1L
)

Arguments

...

(optional) Arguments forwarded, as written, to .method (or to handler), which evaluates them itself with the data as data. Typically the formula appears first (e.g., Y ~ Z); without a handler, these must include whatever .method needs. A legacy model = argument is read as .method with a deprecation warning rather than forwarded.

.method

(optional) The model-fitting function. Defaults to estimatr::lm_robust(), as in declare_estimator().

.summary

(optional) Function used to tidy .method's output. Defaults to tidy_try().

term

(optional) Which model terms to report. A character vector keeps exactly those terms, in that order, and errors if any is absent from the tidied output; TRUE keeps every term including the intercept. When left unset (or FALSE), only the first non-intercept term is reported, so declare_estimator(Y ~ Z + X) returns the Z row alone; a handler's table is kept whole unless term names terms. Evaluated on every draw, so it may name a design parameter.

label

(optional) Step label. Defaults to "test". When two estimator or test steps in one design share a label, + relabels them from their formulas, with a message.

handler

(optional) A function. When supplied, the test bypasses .method and .summary and instead calls handler(data, ...) with the dots as written, not evaluated; it must return a tidy table.

draws

(optional) Number of nested draws for this step. Defaults to 1. When > 1, the step is re-executed draws times for each upstream draw during nested simulation.

Value

A design_step, as declare_estimator() returns, whose estimates carry no inquiry column.

See also

Other design declarations: declare_assignment(), declare_estimator(), declare_inquiry(), declare_measurement(), declare_model(), declare_notes(), declare_parameters(), declare_sampling(), declare_step()

Examples

design <- declare_model(N = 30, Z = rep(0:1, 15), Y = Z + rnorm(N)) +
  declare_test(Y ~ Z, term = "Z", label = "diff")
draw_estimates(design)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 10
#>   term  estimate std.error statistic p.value conf.low conf.high    df outcome
#>   <chr>    <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl> <dbl> <chr>  
#> 1 Z         1.09     0.389      2.79 0.00940    0.288      1.88    28 Y      
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: estimator <chr>
